title: Priv EKS control plane terraform lifecycle safety-kit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions Redwood's private EKS control plane with upgrade-safe lifecycle primitives and automated post-upgrade health verification. The module must be idempotent, produce deterministic outputs for downstream components (kubeconfig SSM path, control-plane instance ARNs, cluster metadata), and include hooks for preflight validations, canary/blue-green upgrade orchestration, and automated rollback triggers based on health probes. The intent is to provide a single module teams can use for VPC/on-prem private deployments that integrates with our Console rollout policies and existing provisioning operator.
acceptance_criteria: Module can create an EKS control plane and required supporting resources (IAM, networking attachments, KMS key alias) using only Terraform
Module exposes outputs: cluster_name, control_plane_kubeconfig_ssm_path, control_plane_role_arn, control_plane_certificate_arn
Upgrade path supports: planned immutable replacement, canary attach, post-upgrade verification window, and automated rollback if health checks fail
Preflight validations run as a Terraform validate/apply plan check and surface human-readable failure reasons
Post-upgrade health-check runner executes a configurable set of probes (api-server liveness, node join rate, control-plane cert age, etc.) and fails the apply if checks do not pass within timeout
Module contains an automated smoke-test Terraform submodule used by CI to validate new releases in a transient sandbox VPC
Comprehensive docs and example usage for Dedicated and Private deployments are published in the infra repo README
Module supports optional customer KMS/HSM integration flags and documents security implications
tasks: Design public API for module (inputs/outputs and lifecycle strategy) and share with infra/PM/design for review
Implement core Terraform resources and patterns (EKS cluster resource, IAM roles, KMS key alias, SSM kubeconfig storage)
Add preflight validators (CIDR checks, subnet tagging, required IAM permissions) as data-driven checks
Implement upgrade strategy primitives: immutable-controlplane boolean, canary-weighting hook, attach/detach lifecycle hooks
Build post-upgrade health-check runner (Terraform external provisioner calling a small Go binary) and integrate with apply-time guard
Create CI job that runs the smoke-test submodule in ephemeral account/VPC and reports pass/fail
Write unit/integration tests and a step-by-step runbook for operators
Prepare API docs, example configs, and migration notes for existing clusters
Open PR, address reviews, and shepherd into release runtime-1.18 or console-2025.03 depending on timing
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after architecture session with Platform and PM. Initial scope focuses on Terraform-only happy path plus a small binary for health probes.
2025-02-12 Priya Kapoor: Reviewed the proposed inputs. Suggest adding a flag for managed nodegroup vs external autoscaling integration to handle Dedicated customers.
2025-02-14 Jordan Blake (PM): Please include a migration path for clusters created by the legacy eks-bootstrapper; we want teams to opt-in to the safety-kit without full reprovision.
2025-02-16 Luca Moreno: PoC branch created: feature/ENG-438271/lifecycle-safetykit. Implemented KMS alias, basic cluster resource and SSM kubeconfig write. Opening draft PR soon.

2025-02-18 Tomás Rivera (Security): Quick review — need to add a documented KMS key policy template for cross-account rotation and to ensure CMKs are not inadvertently shared. Also request security_review_required=true on this ticket.

2025-02-20 Luca Moreno: Added post-upgrade probe runner that checks apiserver readiness, control-plane certificate expiry, and kubelet join rate. Hooked runner into Terraform external data source to fail apply when thresholds exceeded. Running CI now against ephemeral sandbox.

2025-02-22 Priya Kapoor: Design review notes — prefer explicit canary lifecycle separate from immutable replacement to reduce blast radius. Also requested example for blue-green attach/detach flow in docs.
notes: Prefer lightweight Go binary for probes to keep Terraform pure-state limited; evaluate whether AWS SSM Run Command or Step Functions are better fit for long-running verification windows. Keep module surface small so Dedicated customers can still inject provider-specific patches.
